Summary: A judge is not to be reviled — spoken of with contempt — even by one who believes the judgment wrong.
Application: Cursing invokes evil; reviling heaps contempt. This mitzvah covers the contemptuous word itself, guarding the dignity of judgment even when a litigant is aggrieved. Disagreement is pursued by appeal and argument, not by reviling.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: the judge's office bears God-given authority, so reviling him dishonours the order God set. Scripture states the prohibition without a separate reason (Exodus 22:28).
